1
禁軍上
The Palace Corps, Part I
2
宋之兵制，大概有三：天子之衛兵，以守京師，備征戍，曰禁軍； 諸州之鎮兵，以分給役使，曰廂軍； 選於戶籍或應募，使之團結訓練，以爲在所防守，則曰鄉兵。 又有蕃兵，其法始于國初，具籍塞下，團結以爲藩籬之兵； 其後分隊伍，給旗幟，繕營堡，備器械，一律以鄉兵之制。 今因舊史纂修《兵志》，特置於熙寧保甲之前，而附之鄉兵焉。
The Song military establishment falls broadly into three categories: imperial guard troops stationed to defend the capital and stand ready for campaign and frontier service—these are the Palace Corps; prefectural garrison forces detailed for assorted corvée and labor duties—the Comforter Corps; men drawn from household registers or recruited locally, then organized and drilled for defense in their own districts—the Local Militia. There were also frontier tribal troops. The practice began in the early dynasty: men beyond the passes were registered and organized as a defensive screen along the border; later they were formed into units, issued banners and standards, their camps and forts repaired, and arms provided—all governed by the same rules as the Local Militia. In compiling the Military Treatises from the earlier histories, we place this material before the Xining-era baojia reforms and group it with the Local Militia.
3
其軍政，則有召募、揀選、廩給、訓練、屯戍、遷補、器甲、馬政八者之目，條分而著之，以見歷朝因革損益之不同，而世道之盛衰亦具是矣。
Military administration is treated under eight headings—recruitment, selection, rations, training, garrison duty, promotion and replacement, arms and armor, and horse administration—each explained in turn, so that one may see how policy shifted from reign to reign and how the fortunes of the age rose and fell with it.
4
嗟乎！ 三代遠矣。 秦、漢而下得寓兵于農之遺意者，惟唐府衛爲近之。 府衛變而召募，因循姑息，至於藩鎮盛而唐以亡。 更曆五代，亂亡相踵，未有不由於兵者。 太祖起戎行，有天下，收四方勁兵，列營京畿，以備宿衛，分番屯戍，以捍邊圉。 于時將帥之臣入奉朝請，獷暴之民收隸尺籍，雖有桀驁恣肆，而無所施於其間。 凡其制，爲什長之法，階級之辨，使之內外相維，上下相制，截然而不可犯者，是雖以矯累朝藩鎮之弊，而其所懲者深矣。
Alas! The age of the Three Dynasties lies impossibly distant. From Qin and Han onward, only the Tang fubing system came close to preserving the ancient ideal of soldiers living among the farmers who supported them. When the fubing gave way to hired recruitment, indulgence and drift set in, until the military commissioners grew too strong and the Tang fell. Across the Five Dynasties, chaos and collapse followed in unbroken succession—and in every case the army was at the root of it. Taizu rose from military life to win the realm. He gathered the best troops from every quarter, encamped them around the capital as palace guards, and rotated them in turn to the frontiers to hold the borders. Commanders then came to court to pay homage; the violent and unruly were enrolled in the rolls. However fierce or defiant they might be, they had no room left to act on it. The system as a whole set squad leaders over every ten men, fixed ranks and grades, and bound men to one another inside and out and up and down—so tightly that no line could be crossed. It was meant to cure the plague of military commissioners, and the warning it carried was a stern one.
5
咸平以後，承平既久，武備漸寬。 仁宗之世，西兵招刺太多，將驕士惰，徒耗國用，憂世之士屢以爲言，竟莫之改。 神宗奮然更制，於是聯比其民以爲保甲，部分諸路以隸將兵，雖不能盡拯其弊，而亦足以作一時之氣。 時其所任者，王安石也。 元祐、紹聖遵守成憲。 迨崇甯、大觀間，增額日廣而乏精銳，故無益于靖康之變。 時其所任者，童貫也。 建炎南渡，收潰卒，招群盜，以開元帥府。 其初兵不滿萬，用張、韓、劉、岳爲將，而軍聲以振。 及秦檜主和議，士氣遂沮。 孝宗有志興復而未能。 光、寧以後，募兵雖衆，土宇日蹙，況上無馭將之術，而將有中制之嫌。 然沿邊諸壘，尚能戮力效忠，相與維持至百五十年而後亡。 雖其祖宗深仁厚澤有以固結人心，而制兵之有道，綜理之周密，於此亦可見矣。
After the Xianping era, peace had lasted so long that military discipline slowly relaxed. Under Renzong, western recruitment by impressment ran too high; generals grew arrogant and soldiers slack, draining the treasury for little gain. Critics warned of it repeatedly, yet the practice never changed. Shenzong set out boldly to remake the system: households were linked into baojia, and the circuits reorganized under commanders of generals and troops. The abuses were not wholly cured, but for a time the reform revived the army's morale. The man in charge then was Wang Anshi. Under the Yuanyou and Shaosheng reigns, the established rules were kept in force. By the Chongning and Daguan years, quotas swelled while quality fell, and when the Jingkang disaster struck, the army was of no use. The man in charge then was Tong Guan. After the Jianyan flight south, the court took in routed troops, enlisted bandit bands, and set up marshal headquarters. At first there were fewer than ten thousand men; with Zhang, Han, Liu, and Yue in command, the army's reputation revived. Once Qin Hui took charge of the peace talks, the army's spirit collapsed. Xiaozong burned to recover the north but never succeeded. After Guangzong and Ningzong, recruitment swelled even as territory shrank; the throne lacked skill in commanding generals, and generals in turn feared meddling from the court. Even so, the frontier garrisons fought on in loyalty together and kept the dynasty alive for a hundred and fifty years before the end. The founders' deep benevolence surely helped bind hearts to the dynasty—but that they knew how to control armies and administer them with care is plain from this record as well.
6
禁兵者，天子之衛兵也，殿前、侍衛二司總之。 其最親近扈從者，號諸班直，其次總於御前忠佐軍頭司、皇城司、騏驥院。 余皆以守京師、備征伐。 其在外者，非屯駐、屯泊，則就糧軍也。 太祖鑒前代之失，萃精銳于京師，雖曰增損舊制，而規模巨集遠矣。
The Palace Corps were the emperor's own guard, commanded jointly by the Palace Front and Palace Interior bureaus. The closest personal escorts were the various Direct Companies; other units fell under the Loyal Assistants before the Throne, the Imperial City Bureau, and the Fine Steeds Office. All the rest guarded the capital and stood ready for war. Those stationed outside the capital were either in permanent garrison, in temporary camp, or on local grain-pay service. Taizu learned from earlier dynasties' mistakes and massed the best troops in the capital. Later reigns trimmed or expanded the old framework, but the grand design endured.
7
乾德二年，詔遼州降軍宜以效順、懷恩爲名。 三年四月，詔改西川感化、耀武等軍並爲虎捷。 九月，上御講武殿閱諸道兵，得萬餘人，以騎兵爲驍雄，步軍爲雄武，並隸侍衛司，且命王繼勳主之，給緡錢俾娶妻。 繼勳縱之白日掠人妻女，街使不能禁。 帝聞大怒，捕斬者百人，小黃門閻承翰見而不奏，亦杖數十。
In Qiande 2, an edict named the surrendered troops of Liaozhou the Loyal Submission and Grateful Favor commands. In the fourth month of year 3, an edict renamed the Transformation, Dazzling Martial, and other western Sichuan armies Tiger Swift. In the ninth month the emperor reviewed troops from every circuit at the Hall of Martial Instruction. More than ten thousand were chosen: cavalry became Fierce Champions, infantry Bold Warriors, all under the Palace Interior Bureau. Wang Jixun was put in command and given silk cash so the men could marry. Jixun let his men seize wives and daughters in broad daylight, and the street patrols could not stop them. The emperor flew into a rage, had a hundred seized and executed, and had the junior eunuch Yan Chenghan beaten dozens of strokes for seeing the outrage and failing to report it.
8
開寶七年，泰甯軍節度使李從善部下及江南水軍凡千三十九人，並黥面隸籍，以歸化、歸聖爲額。
In Kaibao 7, the 1,039 men under Taining commissioner Li Congshan and the Jiangnan naval force were tattooed and enrolled under the Return to Transformation and Return to Sageliness commands.
9
太平興國二年，詔改簇御馬直曰簇御龍直，鐵騎曰日騎，龍捷曰龍衛，控鶴曰天武，虎捷曰神衛，骨钅朵子直曰御龍骨朵子直，寬衣控鶴曰寬衣天武，雄威曰雄勇，龍騎曰雄猛。 八年，改濮州平海指揮爲崇武。
In Taiping Xingguo 2, an edict renamed Clustered Imperial Horse Direct as Clustered Imperial Dragon Direct, Iron Cavalry as Sun Cavalry, Dragon Swift as Dragon Guard, Crane Control as Heavenly Martial, Tiger Swift as Divine Guard, Mace Direct as Imperial Dragon Mace Direct, Loose-Robe Crane Control as Loose-Robe Heavenly Martial, Bold Prestige as Bold Courage, and Dragon Cavalry as Bold Fierce. In year 8, the Pinghai command of Puzhou was renamed Reverent Martial.
10
雍熙四年，改殿前司日騎钅屈直指揮爲捧日钅屈直，日騎改爲捧日，驍猛改爲拱辰，雄勇改爲神勇，上鐵林改爲殿前司虎翼，腰弩改爲神射，侍衛步軍司鐵林改爲侍衛司虎翼。
In Yongxi 4, the Palace Front Sun Cavalry Bent Bow Direct became Sun-Holding Bent Bow Direct; Sun Cavalry became Sun-Holding; Bold Fierce became Bowing to the Stars; Bold Courage became Divine Courage; Upper Iron Forest became Palace Front Tiger Wing; Waist Crossbow became Divine Archer; and the Palace Interior Infantry Iron Forest became Palace Interior Tiger Wing.
11
至道元年，帝閱禁兵有挽強弩至一石五鬥，連二十發而有餘力者，顧謂左右曰：「今宇內阜安，材武間出，弧矢之妙，亦近代罕有也。 」又令騎步兵各數百，東西列陣，挽強彀弩，視其進退發矢如一，容止中節，因曰：「此殿庭間數百人爾，猶兵威可觀，況堂堂之陣數萬成列者乎！」
In Zhidao 1, reviewing the Palace Corps, the emperor found men who could draw heavy crossbows to one stone five dou and loose twenty bolts in a row with strength to spare. He turned to his attendants and said, "The realm is at peace, yet martial talent still appears; such mastery of bow and crossbow is rare in our own time. " He then had several hundred cavalry and infantry form ranks east and west, draw their crossbows, and advance and retire as one, every movement in measure. He said, "These are only a few hundred men in the palace court, yet their martial bearing is already imposing—what of an army of tens of thousands in full battle order!"
12
咸平三年，詔定州等處本城廳子、無敵、忠銳、定塞指揮，已並升充禁軍馬軍雲翼指揮，依逐州軍就糧，令侍衛馬軍司管轄。 定州揀中廳子第一充雲翼第一，第二充雲翼第二； 相州廳子第一充雲翼第三，第二充雲翼第四； 保州無敵第一充雲翼第五，第二充雲翼第六，忠銳充雲翼第七； 威勇軍無敵第一充雲翼第八，第二充雲翼第九，忠銳充雲翼第十； 靜戎軍無敵充雲翼第十一； 甯邊軍無敵充雲翼第十二； 北平塞無敵充雲翼第十三； 深州無敵充雲翼第十四。 北面諸處應管本城、定塞指揮已下鎮定州、高陽關路都總管，並充禁軍馬軍雲翼指揮，才候升立訖，分析逐指揮員兵士人數、就糧州府、本指揮見在去處以聞。
In Xianping 3, an edict promoted the Hall Sons, Invincible, Loyal Sharp, and Secure the Frontier commands of Dingzhou and other posts to Palace Corps cavalry Cloud Wing commands, paid grain locally in each prefecture, under the Palace Interior Cavalry Bureau. At Dingzhou, the first selected Hall Sons unit became Cloud Wing First, the second Cloud Wing Second; at Xiangzhou, Hall Sons First became Cloud Wing Third and Second Cloud Wing Fourth; at Baozhou, Invincible First became Cloud Wing Fifth, Second Cloud Wing Sixth, and Loyal Sharp Cloud Wing Seventh; at Weiyong, Invincible First became Cloud Wing Eighth, Second Cloud Wing Ninth, and Loyal Sharp Cloud Wing Tenth; at Jingrong, Invincible became Cloud Wing Eleventh; at Ningbian, Invincible became Cloud Wing Twelfth; at Beiping Stockade, Invincible became Cloud Wing Thirteenth; at Shenzhou, Invincible became Cloud Wing Fourteenth. All local garrison and Secure the Frontier commands and below on the northern frontier under the Dingzhou and Gaoyang Pass routes were likewise promoted to Palace Corps cavalry Cloud Wing commands; once promotion was complete, each command's strength, grain-pay prefecture, and present station were to be reported.
13
四年，詔陝西沿邊州軍兵士先選中者，並升爲禁軍，名保捷。 五年正月，置廣捷兵士五指揮。 五月，命使臣分往邠、寧、環、慶、涇、原、儀、渭、隴、鄜、延等州，於保安、保毅軍內，與逐處官吏選取有力者共二萬人，各於本州置營，升爲禁軍，號曰振武指揮。 既而帝曰：「邊防闕兵，朝廷須爲制置，蓋不得已也。 候邊鄙乂寧，即可銷弭。 」六月，以河東州兵爲神銳二十四指揮、神虎十指揮，又升石州廳子軍爲禁軍，又以威虎十指揮隸虎翼。
In year 4, an edict promoted all previously selected frontier troops in Shaanxi to Palace Corps under the name Secure Swift. In the first month of year 5, five Broad Swift commands were established. In the fifth month, envoys were dispatched to Bin, Ning, Huan, Qing, Jing, Yuan, Yi, Wei, Long, Fu, and Yan to work with local officials in selecting 20,000 able men from the Secure Peace and Secure Resolution forces, camp them in each prefecture, and promote them to Palace Corps as Quake Martial commands. The emperor then said, "The frontier lacks troops, and the court must provide for it—there is no choice. When the border is calm again, they can be disbanded." " In the sixth month, Hedong prefectural troops became twenty-four Divine Sharp and ten Divine Tiger commands; the Shizhou Hall Sons army was promoted to Palace Corps, and ten Bold Tiger commands were attached to Tiger Wing.
14
景德四年，詔河東廣銳、神銳、神虎軍以見存爲定額，缺則補之。
In Jingde 4, an edict fixed the present strength of the Hedong Broad Sharp, Divine Sharp, and Divine Tiger armies as permanent quotas, with vacancies filled as they arose.
15
康定初，趙元昊反，西邊用兵，詔募神捷兵，易名萬勝，爲營二十。 所募多市井選忄耎，不足以備戰守。 是時禁兵多戍陝西，並邊土兵雖不及等，然驍勇善戰。 京師所遣戍者，雖稱魁頭，大率不能辛苦，而摧鋒陷陣非其所長。 又北兵戍及川峽、荊湘、嶺嶠間，多不便習水土，故議者欲益募土兵爲就糧。 於是增置陝西蕃落、保捷、定功，河北雲翼、有馬勁勇，陝西、河北振武，河北、京東武衛，陝西、京西壯勇，延州青澗，登州澄海弩手，京畿近郡亦增募龍騎、廣勇、廣捷、虎翼、步鬥、步武，復升河北招收、無敵、廳子馬，陝西制勝，并州克戎、騎射，麟州飛騎，府州威遠，秦州建威，慶州有馬安塞，保州威邊，安肅軍忠銳，嵐、府州建安，登州平海，皆爲禁兵，增內外馬步凡數百營。 又京東西、河北、河東、江、淮、荊湖、兩浙、福建路各募宣毅，大州二營，小州一營，凡二百八十八。 岢嵐軍別置床子弩炮手。 時吏以所募多寡爲賞罰格，諸軍子弟悉聽隸籍，禁軍闕額多選本城補填，故慶曆中外禁、廂軍總一百二十五萬，視國初爲最多。 西師既罷，上患兵冗，帑庾不能給，乃詔省兵數萬人。
Early in the Kangding era, Zhao Yuanhao rebelled and war opened on the western frontier. An edict recruited Divine Swift troops, renamed them Myriad Victor, and formed twenty camps. Most recruits were timid men picked from the marketplace, unfit for real fighting or garrison duty. Most Palace Corps then garrisoned Shaanxi. Frontier local troops ranked below them, yet they fought with greater dash and skill. Capital troops sent west were called the elite, but most could not endure hardship and were poor at leading charges. Northern troops posted to Sichuan, the Jing-Xiang region, and the far south often sickened in alien climates, so reformers urged recruiting more local grain-pay militia. New Palace Corps units followed across the realm: Tribal Frontier, Secure Swift, and Secure Merit in Shaanxi; Cloud Wing and Strong Steed with Horses in Hebei; Quake Martial in Shaanxi and Hebei; Martial Guard in Hebei and the eastern capital region; Bold Courage in Shaanxi and the western capital region; Qingjian at Yanzhou; Clear Sea crossbowmen at Dengzhou; and in the capital region Dragon Cavalry, Broad Courage, Broad Swift, Tiger Wing, Infantry Combat, and Infantry Martial. Hebei Reception, Invincible, and Hall Sons cavalry, Shaanxi Overcome Foe, Bingzhou Subdue Barbarians and Mounted Archers, Linzhou Flying Cavalry, Fuzhou Awesome Distance, Qinzhou Establish Prestige, Qingzhou Mounted Secure Frontier, Baozhou Awesome Border, Ansu Loyal Sharp, Lan-Fu Jian'an, and Dengzhou Pinghai were all promoted as well—adding several hundred horse and foot camps in all. Loyal Display units were also recruited in the eastern and western capital regions, Hebei, Hedong, Jiang-Huai, Jing-Hu, the two Zhe circuits, and Fujian—two camps in large prefectures, one in small—for 288 camps in all. At Kelan Army a separate corps of bed-frame crossbow and artillery crews was added. Officials were judged by how many men they recruited; soldiers' sons were enrolled freely; Palace Corps gaps were filled from local garrisons. By the Qingli era Palace and Comforter Corps together numbered 1.25 million—the peak since the founding. When the western war ended, the emperor worried that the army had grown too large for the treasury to sustain and ordered tens of thousands cut.
16
皇祐二年，川峽增置寧遠。 五年，江、淮、荊湖置教閱忠節，州一營，大州五百人，小州三百人。 於是宣毅浸廢不復補，而荊湖、廣南益募雄略。 至和二年，廣、桂、邕州置有馬雄略。 明年，並萬勝爲十營。 其後，議者謂東南雖無事，不宜馳備。 嘉祐四年，乃詔荊南、江寧府、揚、廬、洪、潭、福、越州募就糧軍，號威果，各營於本州。 又益遣禁軍駐泊，長吏兼本路兵馬鈐轄，選武臣爲都監，專主訓練。 於是東南稍有備矣。
In Huangyou 2, the Secure Distance command was added in Sichuan. In year 5, Jiang-Huai and Jing-Hu gained Loyal Integrity drill units—one camp per prefecture, 500 men in large prefectures and 300 in small. Loyal Display units were then allowed to lapse without replacement, while Jing-Hu and Guangnan recruited more Bold Strategy troops. In Zhihe 2, Mounted Bold Strategy units were established in Guang, Gui, and Yong prefectures. The following year, Myriad Victor was consolidated into ten camps. Later critics argued that even though the southeast was at peace, defenses there should not be neglected. In Jiayou 4, an edict recruited grain-pay troops at Jingnan, Jiangning, Yang, Lu, Hong, Tan, Fu, and Yue under the name Awesome Fruit, each camped in its home prefecture. More Palace Corps were posted in temporary garrison; prefects doubled as circuit military commissioners, and martial officials were chosen as chief supervisors devoted to training. The southeast was at last somewhat prepared.
17
七年，宰相韓琦言：
In the seventh year, Chief Councilor Han Qi memorialized:
18
祖宗以兵定天下，凡有征戍則募置，事已則並，故兵日精而用不廣。 今二邊雖號通好，而西北屯邊之兵，常若待敵之至，故竭天下之力而不能給。 不於此時先慮而豫備之，一旦邊陲用兵，水旱相繼，卒起而圖之，不可及矣。
The founders won the realm by force of arms. Whenever campaign or garrison duty arose, they recruited troops; when the task ended, those units were merged back—so the army grew sharper while costs stayed contained. Today both frontiers are said to be at peace, yet northwestern garrisons stand as if the enemy might strike at any moment—and the empire exhausts itself and still cannot pay for them. If we do not plan and prepare now, then when war breaks on the frontier and flood and drought follow in turn, any sudden remedy will come too late.
19
又三路就糧之兵雖勇勁服習，然邊儲貴踴，常苦難贍。 若其數過多，復有尾大不掉之患。 京師之兵雖雜且少精，然漕于東南，廣而易供設，其數多，得強幹弱枝之勢。 祖宗時，就糧之兵不甚多，邊陲有事，則以京師兵益之，其慮深而其費鮮。 願詔樞密院同三司量河北、陝西、河東及三司榷貨務歲入金帛之數，約可贍京師及三路兵馬幾何，然後以可贍之數立爲定額。 額外罷募，闕即增補。 額外數已盡而營畸零，則省並之。 既見定額，則可以定其路馬步軍一營，以若干爲額。 仍請核見開寶、至道、天禧、慶曆中外兵馬之數。 蓋開寶、至道之兵，太祖、太宗以之定天下、服四方也。 天禧之兵，真宗所以守成備豫也。 慶曆之兵，西師後增置之數也。 以祖宗之兵，視今數之多少，則精冗易判，裁制無疑矣。
Grain-pay troops on the three frontier routes are brave and well trained, yet frontier supplies are costly and hard to sustain. If their numbers grow too large, we risk the old problem of a tail too heavy for the body to command. Capital troops, though mixed and not all elite, are fed by grain transport from the southeast—ample and easy to supply—and their numbers give the court a strong trunk and weak branches. Under the founders, grain-pay troops were few; when the frontier needed help, capital troops were sent to reinforce them—far-sighted policy at modest cost. I ask that the Bureau of Military Affairs and the State Finance Commission calculate annual revenue in gold and silk from Hebei, Shaanxi, Hedong, and the Monopoly Goods Offices, estimate how much can sustain the capital and the three frontier routes, and then fix troop strength to what revenue can bear. Beyond the quota, stop recruiting; fill vacancies only as they occur. When the excess is gone but undersized camps remain, merge and abolish them. Once the quota is fixed, each route's horse and foot camps can be set at a standard strength. I also ask that troop strength under Kaibao, Zhidao, Tianxi, and Qingli be verified. The Kaibao and Zhidao armies were those with which Taizu and Taizong won the realm and subdued the four quarters. The Tianxi armies were those Zhenzong kept to guard the achievement and stay prepared. The Qingli armies were the forces added after the western war. Compare the founders' armies with today's numbers, and it will be easy to see whether we are lean or bloated—and to cut without hesitation.
20
於是詔中書、樞密院同議。 樞密院奏：開寶之籍總三十七萬八千，而禁軍馬步十九萬三千； 至道之籍總六十六萬六千，而禁軍馬步三十五萬八千； 天禧之籍總九十一萬二千，而禁軍馬步四十三萬二千； 慶曆之籍總一百二十五萬九千，而禁軍馬步八十二萬六千。 視前所募後浸多，自是稍加裁制，以爲定額。
An edict then ordered the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs to deliberate together. The Bureau of Military Affairs reported: under Kaibao, registers totaled 378,000 men, including 193,000 Palace Corps cavalry and infantry; under Zhidao, 666,000 in all, of whom 358,000 were Palace Corps cavalry and infantry; under Tianxi, 912,000 in all, of whom 432,000 were Palace Corps cavalry and infantry; under Qingli, 1,259,000 in all, of whom 826,000 were Palace Corps cavalry and infantry. Recruitment had gradually swelled beyond earlier levels; from this point the court trimmed slightly and fixed a permanent quota.
21
三年十二月，樞密使文彥博等上在京、開封府界及京東等路禁軍數，帝亦參以治平中兵數而討論焉。 遂詔：殿前虎翼除水軍一指揮外，存六十指揮，各以五百人爲率，總三萬四百人； 在京增廣勇五指揮，共二千人； 開封府界定六萬二千人，京東五萬一千二百人，兩浙四千人，江東五千二百人，江西六千八百人，湖南八千三百人，湖北萬二千人，福建四千五百人，廣南東、西千二百人，川峽三路四千四百人爲額。 在京其餘指揮並河東、陝西、京西、淮南路既皆撥並，唯河北人數尚多，乃詔禁軍以七萬爲額。 初，河北兵籍比諸路爲多，其緣邊者且仰給三司，至是而撥並畸零，立爲定額焉。 是時，京東增置武衛軍，分隸河北四路，後又以三千人戍揚、杭州、江寧府，其後又團結軍士置將分領，則謂之將兵雲。
In the twelfth month of the third year, Military Affairs Commissioner Wen Yanbo and others submitted Palace Corps strength in the capital, the Kaifeng metropolitan jurisdiction, and routes such as Jingdong; the emperor also weighed these against Zhiping-era troop figures in discussion. An edict followed: of Palace Front Tiger Wing, aside from one naval command, sixty commands were retained, each at five hundred men, 30,400 in all; in the capital five Broad Courage commands were added, two thousand men in all; quotas were set at 62,000 for the Kaifeng metropolitan jurisdiction, 51,200 for Jingdong, 4,000 for Two Zhe, 5,200 for Jiangdong, 6,800 for Jiangxi, 8,300 for Hunan, 12,000 for Hubei, 4,500 for Fujian, 1,200 for Guangnan East and West, and 4,400 for the three Sichuan routes. In the capital, remaining commands and those of Hedong, Shaanxi, Jingxi, and Huainan had already been reassigned and merged; only Hebei still exceeded the norm, so an edict fixed Palace Corps there at seventy thousand. At first Hebei's registers outnumbered every other route; frontier units moreover depended on the State Finance Commission for supplies. Now scattered detachments were reassigned and merged, and a fixed quota was set. At this time Jingdong raised Martial Guard armies and distributed them among Hebei's four routes; later three thousand men garrisoned Yangzhou, Hangzhou, and Jiangning Prefecture; still later soldiers were grouped under generals in separate commands—these were called commander troops.
22
